slides.title: Learning with Labels
slides.rawText: ))} What is Supervised Learning? Learning with Labels Supervised learning is a machine learning approach where the model learns from labeled training data. Each example has an input and the correct output. Teacher-Student Analogy Think of it like a teacher providing answers. The model (student) learns to map inputs to outputs by studying these labeled examples. Goal: Prediction After training, the model can predict the correct output for new, unseen inputs based on patterns it learned from the labeled data.

slides.title: Classification
slides.rawText: ))} Two Main Types Classification Predict discrete categories or classes Binary: Yes/No, Spam/Not Spam Multi-class: Cat/Dog/Bird Output: Class label Regression Predict continuous numerical values House prices Temperature prediction Output: Number Key difference: Classification predicts categories, Regression predicts numbers

slides.title: Email Spam Detection
slides.rawText: ))} Real-World Examples Email Spam Detection Classifies emails as spam or not spam based on content, sender, and patterns House Price Prediction Predicts house prices based on location, size, amenities, and market trends Credit Card Fraud Identifies fraudulent transactions by learning from past fraud patterns Medical Diagnosis Assists in disease diagnosis by analyzing patient symptoms and test results

slides.title: 1. Collect Data
slides.rawText: ))} How It Works 1. Collect Data Gather labeled examples with inputs and correct outputs 2. Train Model Model learns patterns by minimizing prediction errors 3. Make Predictions Use trained model to predict outputs for new data Key insight: The quality of labeled data directly impacts model performance

slides.title: Linear Regression
slides.rawText: ))} Common Algorithms Linear Regression Predicts continuous values using a linear relationship Best for: Simple regression tasks Decision Trees Makes decisions by splitting data based on features Best for: Classification and regression Neural Networks Complex models inspired by human brain structure Best for: Complex patterns and large datasets Support Vector Machines Finds optimal hyperplane to separate classes Best for: Classification tasks

slides.title: Labeled Data is Essential
slides.rawText: ))} Key Takeaways Labeled Data is Essential Supervised learning requires labeled examples with inputs and correct outputs to train effectively Two Main Types Classification predicts categories (spam/not spam), Regression predicts numbers (house prices) Widely Used Powers spam filters, recommendation systems, fraud detection, medical diagnosis, and more Remember: Quality labeled data = Better predictions
